title: Giants: Anakim and Rephaim
lead: The Bible remembers tall peoples who lived in Canaan and east of the Jordan before Israel: the Anakim of Hebron, and the groups Deuteronomy calls Rephaim, Emim and Zamzummim. The scouts' fear of them (Numbers 13:33) shaped Israel's story from Kadesh to David and Goliath.

sections.b: The giant peoples appear at several points in the Bible's story. Genesis 14:5 lists the Rephaim, Zuzim and Emim among peoples defeated by eastern kings in Abraham's day. The scouts in Numbers 13:28–33 see the descendants of Anak at Hebron and feel like grasshoppers, and their report keeps Israel out of the land for forty years. Deuteronomy's asides (2:10–12; 2:20–23) say God drove out such peoples before Edom, Moab and Ammon, and Og of Bashan is the last of the Rephaim (Deuteronomy 3:11). Caleb takes Hebron from the three sons of Anak (Joshua 15:13–14), and Joshua 11:21–22 says Anakim were left only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod, the Philistine towns from which Goliath of Gath later comes (1 Samuel 17:4). Other uses of repha'im name the shades of the dead (Isaiah 14:9; Isaiah 26:14). Later Jewish writings linked the giants with the Nephilim of Genesis 6:4; see the fallen angels topic.
